sentences.text: Hon'ble Anish Kumar Gupta,J.

1. Heard Shri Prashant Shukla, learned counsel for the petitioner, Shri Rajiv Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State-respondents and Shri Utkarsh Birla, learned counsel for respondent No. 2.
2.

The instant petition has been filed praying for quashing of the order dated 16.05.2024 and for a direction to the respondents to issue allotment letter to the petitioners for 10% developed land as has been done in the case of co-sharers.

sentences.text: 3. Indisputably, certain land of the petitioner was acquired by Noida Authority under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

An award was declared on 08.11.2001.
4.

The case of the petitioners is that as per the decision of the Authority taken in its 92nd Board meeting dated 07.01.1998, 5% developed abadi land is to be allotted to pushtaini kastkars in lieu of acquisition of their land in addition to compensation.
Again in 154th Board meeting dated 18.09.2008, decision was taken to extend the said benefit to the pushtaini kashtkars of other villages also.
The petitioners had claimed developed land in lieu of acquisition of their land comprising of Khata No. 730, Khasra No. 519M and 521.

By the impugned order, their claim has been rejected on the ground that in spot inspection got done by the Authority, it transpired that the petitioners were in illegal possession over Khasra No. 104 and 124.
Their name is included in the list of ineligible candidates of village Sadarpur on account of being in illegal possession of Khasra No. 104 and 124.
The Lekhpal in a recent inspection got conducted by the Authority has confirmed the illegal possession of the petitioners.
5. It is not disputed by counsel for the Authority that the petitioners are pushtaini kashtkars.

Their claim has been rejected solely on the ground of alleged illegal occupation of Khasra No. 104 and 124.
6.

In paragraph No. 17, the petitioners have set up a specific case to the effect that the aforesaid plots are in illegal possession of Smt. Indra Sharma wife of Chetram and Khajan Singh and Raje sons of Med Singh.

Para-17 of the petition is to the following effect:
"17.
That name of Smt. Indra Sharma wife of Chetram issuing at Khasra No. 104.

That the name of Khajan Singh and Raje who are son of Med Singh are showing at Khasra No. 124, hence the bogus allegation levelled by the respondents against the petitioners are perverse false on the face of record and the respondents can't shy away with their statutory duties."
7. In para-25 of the counter affidavit, the Authority has not specifically denied the assertions made in para-17 of the writ petition.

The only assertion is that the petitioners have not disclosed any sale/purchase of the said land and therefore, the stand taken in para-17 is not acceptable.
8.
Learned counsel for the petitioners vehemently submits that the petitioners are not in possession of the aforesaid plots.
They have disclosed the name of the persons who are in possession of the same.
The petitioners will have no objection in case the Authority proceeds to dispossess the illegal occupants of the aforesaid plots or carries out demolition of constructions existing over it, if any.
It is urged that claim of the petitioners for developed land cannot be denied on basis of aforesaid vague stand.
9. We find the submission to have considerable force.

Once, the petitioners have come up with a categorical case that they are not in possession of Khasra No. 104 and 124, the burden was on the Authority to prove it by positive evidence which they have failed to do.

Moreover, since counsel for the petitioners has made a statement before this Court that the petitioners would have no objection in case the Authority proceeds to dispossess anyone who may be found in possession of the Pratap Singh vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169032575/
2 aforesaid plots or demolishes the constructions existing over it, it amply safeguards the interest of the Authority.

sentences.text: The petitioners cannot be expected to lead negative evidence to prove that they are not in possession of the aforesaid plots.

10. However, the matter does not end here as the Authority in para-25 of the counter affidavit for the first time has come up with a new case that in a recent spot inspection got conducted by it the petitioners have been found to be in illegal possession of Khasra No. 209 and 162.
In the rejoinder affidavit, the petitioners have tried to explain the aforesaid case set up by the Authority.
It is submitted that the aforesaid assertion is made on basis of some ex parte enquiry got conducted by the Authority during pendency of the writ petition without any notice to the petitioners.

11. Since the Authority has come up with a new plea to counter the claim of the petitioners and that too on basis of an enquiry in which the petitioners were not associated and therefore, we are of the opinion that the petitioners are entitled to be heard on the said aspect.
12. Accordingly, the impugned order is hereby quashed.
13. The Authority shall issue notice to the petitioners within two weeks in respect of the alleged illegal encroachment over Khasra No. 209 and 162.
It will also provide all evidence in its possession in support of the said stand so that the petitioners may be in a position to submit effective reply to the same within next four weeks.
The Authority shall pass a fresh order taking into consideration the stand as may be taken by the petitioners in their objection to the notice.
The entire exercise in this behalf shall be completed within twelve weeks from today.
14. In the result, the petition stands allowed to the extent indicated above.

Order Date :- 6.11.2024 Mukesh Kr.
(Anish Kumar Gupta,J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.)
